label: Set translate mode
summary: Switches the court scene editor's tool to translate (move) mode.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button click in the court scene editor window. Going by its name, translate means moving an object; the game documents nothing more.

label: Court type itself
summary: Hands back the court type object it is called on, for passing on to other functions.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the court type itself. Vanilla has no use of it on this type, so this rests on the name only.

label: Court type effects text
summary: The text that describes what a court type does.
details: Vanilla puts it in the general court type tooltip, below the court type's own description.

label: Court type name
summary: The name of the court type, as text.
details: Going by its name and the many uses of GetName on other types, it returns the display name. Vanilla's own lines here belong to other types, so this rests on the name.

label: Court type name, plain
summary: The name of the court type as plain text, without a hover tooltip attached.
details: Vanilla uses it as the text of a label in the shared tooltip layout (cooltip.gui).

label: Court type description
summary: The descriptive text of a court type, shown in its tooltip.
details: Vanilla puts it first in the general court type tooltip, followed by the effects text.

label: Court type itself
summary: The court type object itself, for passing it to other functions.
details: Going by its name, and by how other types use Self (for example Character.Self as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Court type entry itself
summary: Hands back the court type list entry it is called on, for passing on to other functions.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the entry itself. Vanilla has no use of it on this type, so this rests on the name only.

label: Can afford court type
summary: Whether the cost of switching to this court type can be paid.
details: Vanilla enables the court type button only when this is true, together with the entry being valid and not already the active court type. Going by its name, it checks the cost; who pays is not shown in the input.

label: Cannot select tooltip
summary: The tooltip text that explains why this court type cannot be chosen.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the court types window.

label: Court type background
summary: The background picture of this court type entry.
details: Going by its name, it returns a texture. Vanilla has no use of it on this type; lines of other types use a GetBackground as a picture, which is only a hint.

label: Confirm change tooltip
summary: The tooltip text shown for confirming a change to this court type.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the court types window.

label: Court type cost
summary: The cost of switching to this court type, written as text.
details: Vanilla shows it after the word Cost in the change court type text.

label: Court type entry description
summary: The description text of this court type entry.
details: Going by its name, it returns a description. Vanilla has no use of it on this type; lines of other types use a GetDescription for descriptions, which is only a hint.

label: Court type entry name
summary: The name of this court type entry, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in the warning that you cannot switch back to your current court type after adopting a new one.

label: Court type entry name, plain
summary: The name of this court type entry as plain text, without a hover tooltip attached.
details: Vanilla uses it as label text in the court types window.

label: Is shown
summary: Whether this court type entry is shown in the list.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility of one element, and, negated and combined with IsValid, as the visibility of another element when the entry is not shown or not valid.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether this court type entry is valid.
details: Vanilla shows an element only when it is false, and enables the court type button only when it is true. What makes an entry invalid is not shown in the input.

label: Court type entry itself
summary: The court type list entry itself, for passing it to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it to the select function when an entry is clicked, and compares it with the currently selected entry to highlight it.

label: Court type window itself
summary: Hands back the court type window it is called on, for passing on to other functions.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the window itself. Vanilla has no use of it on this type, so this rests on the name only.

label: Confirm court type change
summary: Carries out the court type change the player has selected.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button click in the court types window. Going by its name, it completes the change; the game documents nothing more.

label: Active court type entry
summary: The list entry of the court type the player's court currently has.
details: Vanilla reads its name for the court type button and its tooltip. The input does not show what else can be read from it.

label: Court type entries
summary: The list of court type entries to show in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of the list in the court types window, so one row is made per entry.

label: Selected court type entry
summary: The court type entry currently selected in the window.
details: Vanilla compares it with each entry to highlight the selected one. Going by its name and the select and finalize functions beside it, it is probably a pending choice, not yet confirmed.

label: Court owner
summary: The ruler who owns the court shown in this window.
details: Vanilla reads the owner's culture from it. Going by its name, the owner is the character whose court it is.

label: Show or hide tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the button that shows or hides the court type window.
details: Going by its name, it returns a tooltip. Vanilla has no use of it on this type; a council window uses a function of the same name for its own show or hide button, which is only a hint.

label: Is window visible
summary: Whether the court type window is currently open.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility of the window's contents.

label: Select court type
summary: Marks a court type entry as the player's current choice in the window.
details: Vanilla runs it on a click, passing the clicked entry. Going by the name of FinalizeCourtTypeChange, confirming the change is a separate step.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The court type entry to select.
fields.values: a court type entry, as vanilla passes CourtTypeSettingItem.Self

label: Court type window itself
summary: The court type window itself, for passing it to other functions.
details: Going by its name, and by how other types use Self (for example Character.Self as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Show or hide window
summary: Opens the court type window if it is closed, and closes it if it is open.
details: Vanilla runs it from buttons in both the court amenities window and the court types window. Going by its name, it toggles the window's visibility.

label: Court visual entry itself
summary: Hands back the court visual list entry it is called on, for passing on to other functions.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the entry itself. Vanilla has no use of it on this type, so this rests on the name only.

label: Court visual background
summary: The background picture of this court visual option.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of a picture in the court visuals window.

label: Court visual background name
summary: A text value tied to this court visual's background.
details: Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents only that it returns text. What the text holds (a name, a file path) is not known.

label: Court visual description
summary: The description text of this court visual option.
details: Vanilla uses it as text in the court visuals window.

label: Court visual name
summary: The name of this court visual option, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it as text in the court visuals window.

label: Is default visual
summary: Whether this court visual option is the default one.
details: Vanilla uses it to decide when a part of the court visuals window is visible. Going by its name, it marks the default option.

label: Court visual entry itself
summary: The court visual list entry itself, for passing it to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it to the apply function when an entry is clicked, and compares it with the active entry to mark it.

label: Court visuals window itself
summary: Hands back the court visuals window it is called on, for passing on to other functions.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the window itself. Vanilla has no use of it on this type, so this rests on the name only.

label: Apply court visual
summary: Applies the chosen court visual option to the court.
details: Vanilla runs it on a click, passing the clicked entry.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The court visual entry to apply.
fields.values: a court visual entry, as vanilla passes CourtVisualSettingItem.Self

label: Active court visual entry
summary: The court visual entry that is currently applied.
details: Vanilla compares it with each entry to show which one is active.

label: Court visual entries
summary: The list of court visual options to show in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of the list in the court visuals window, so one row is made per entry.

label: Royal court window
summary: The royal court window.
details: Vanilla reads from it whether the visuals tab is the active one (IsActiveVisualsTab), to decide visibility.

label: Reset court visual
summary: Sets the court visual back to the default option.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button click in the court visuals window.

label: Court visuals window itself
summary: The court visuals window itself, for passing it to other functions.
details: Going by its name, and by how other types use Self (for example Character.Self as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Court position window
summary: The court position window that belongs to the court window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the court window, so that part can read the position window's data.

label: Court window itself
summary: Hands back the court window it is called on, for passing on to other functions.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the window itself. Vanilla has no use of it on this type, so this rests on the name only.

label: Can do mass prisoner action
summary: Whether the chosen action can be done on all prisoners at once.
details: Vanilla enables its three buttons with it, passing ransom, release or execute.

label: Close court window
summary: Closes the court window.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button click in the court window.

label: Court
summary: The court shown in the court window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of parts of the court window, so they can read the court's data.

label: Court owner
summary: The ruler whose court the window shows.
details: Vanilla reads custom texts from it, such as the plural of the court position name and whether to say guests, for the window's headings.

label: Mass prisoner action tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for a mass action on all prisoners.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of three buttons, passing ransom, release or execute.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Which action the tooltip is for.

label: Prisoners
summary: The prisoners of the court shown in the window, as a group the window can count.
details: Vanilla reads the total number from it to show a count, and makes a part of the window half transparent when that number is zero.

label: Is court tab shown
summary: Whether the court window currently shows its court tab.
details: Vanilla uses it to mark the tab button as pressed and to change how clicks pass through.

label: Is positions tab shown
summary: Whether the court window currently shows its court positions tab.
details: Vanilla uses it to mark the tab button as pressed and to change how clicks pass through.

label: Is prison tab shown
summary: Whether the court window currently shows its prison tab.
details: Vanilla uses it to mark the tab button as pressed and to change how clicks pass through.

label: Mass prisoner action
summary: Does the chosen action on all prisoners at once.
details: Vanilla runs it from three buttons, passing ransom, release or execute. The exact effect of each is not shown in the input.

label: Court window itself
summary: The court window itself, for passing it to other functions.
details: Going by its name, and by how other types use Self (for example Character.Self as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Show court tab
summary: Switches the court window to its court tab.
details: Vanilla runs it from a tab button click.

label: Show positions tab
summary: Switches the court window to its court positions tab.
details: Vanilla runs it from a tab button click.

label: Show prison tab
summary: Switches the court window to its prison tab.
details: Vanilla runs it from a tab button click.

label: Knights view
summary: The knights part of the create accolade window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a section of the window, so that section can read the knights data.

label: Military view
summary: The military part of the create accolade window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a section of the window, so that section can read the military data.

label: Create accolade window itself
summary: Hands back the create accolade window it is called on, for passing on to other functions.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the window itself. Vanilla has no use of it on this type, so this rests on the name only.

label: Can create accolade
summary: Whether the accolade can be created with the current choices.
details: Vanilla enables the create button only when this is true.

label: Close accolade window
summary: Closes the create accolade window.
details: Vanilla runs it from button clicks in that window.

label: Create accolade
summary: Creates the accolade from the choices made in the window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the create button. Going by the window's other functions, the choices are probably the selected knight, the initial type and the name.

label: Edit accolade name
summary: Reacts to the player typing in the accolade name field.
details: Vanilla runs it when the text of the name field is edited. Going by its name, it takes the typed text as the new temporary name.

label: Accolade name
summary: The name of the accolade being created, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it as text in the create accolade window.

label: Change initial type tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for changing the accolade's initial type.
details: Vanilla never uses it. Going by its name, it returns a tooltip; the game documents nothing more.

label: Rank icon on the bar
summary: The icon for one rank step of a complex progress bar.
details: Vanilla has no use of it on this type. The accolade window uses a function of the same name on its own type, passing the index of a bar item, which suggests the argument is the step's position. That is only a hint.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a number, the position of the bar item (inferred from a use on another type)

label: Rank tooltip on the bar
summary: The tooltip text for one rank step of a complex progress bar.
details: Vanilla has no use of it on this type. The accolade window uses a function of the same name on its own type, passing the index of a bar item, which suggests the argument is the step's position. That is only a hint.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a number, the position of the bar item (inferred from a use on another type)

label: Create accolade tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the create accolade button.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of that button.

label: Liege
summary: A liege (the ruler a character serves) as seen from the create accolade window.
details: Vanilla has no use of it on this type. Going by its name, it is the liege character; lines of other types use a GetLiege that way, which is only a hint.

label: Possible accolade types
summary: The list of accolade types the player can pick from.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of a list in the window, so one row is made per type.

label: Progress bar
summary: A progress bar object for the create accolade window.
details: Vanilla has no use of it on this type. Going by its name, it returns a progress bar; lines of other types use a GetProgressBar as data for a bar, which is only a hint.

label: Selected accolade type
summary: The accolade type the player has picked as the starting type.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a section, and checks its IsValid to show a section or a prompt when nothing is picked.

label: Selected knight
summary: The knight the player has picked in the create accolade window.
details: Vanilla uses its short name in the tooltip texts of the window, for example the one about forbidding that knight from being a knight of the player's culture.

label: Temporary accolade name
summary: The name text typed in the window so far, before it is submitted.
details: Vanilla uses it as the text of the name field. Going by its name, it is the not yet final name.

label: Is changing initial type
summary: Whether the window is in the mode of changing the accolade's initial type.
details: Vanilla never uses it. This rests on the name only.

label: Is changing type
summary: Whether the window is in the mode of changing the accolade's type.
details: Vanilla never uses it. This rests on the name only.

label: Is renaming
summary: Whether the player is currently editing the accolade's name.
details: Vanilla uses it to switch between the shown name and the name edit field.

label: Create accolade window itself
summary: The create accolade window itself, for passing it to other functions.
details: Going by its name, and by how other types use Self (for example Character.Self as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Select accolade type
summary: Picks the accolade type that the accolade starts with.
details: Vanilla runs it on a click, passing the clicked accolade type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: an accolade type, as vanilla passes AccoladeType.Self

label: Select knight
summary: Picks the knight who will receive the accolade.
details: Vanilla runs it on a click, passing the clicked character.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a character, as vanilla passes Character.Self

label: Submit accolade name
summary: Takes the typed name as the accolade's name.
details: Vanilla runs it when the player presses Return in the name field. Going by its name, it submits the typed name.

label: Toggle changing initial type
summary: Switches the window in or out of the mode of changing the initial type.
details: Vanilla never uses it. This rests on the name only.

label: Toggle renaming
summary: Switches the accolade name between display and edit mode.
details: Vanilla runs it from button clicks, next to the IsRenaming check.

label: Create account itself
summary: Hands back the create account object it is called on, for passing on to other functions.
details: A function of the account sign-up in the game's interface. Vanilla has no use of it on this type, so this rests on the name only.

label: Can create account
summary: Whether the account sign-up form can be sent off right now.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable a control of the engine's Paradox account creation window, going by the name the create button. What must be filled in first is not described.

label: Create account
summary: Sends off the account sign-up form to create a Paradox account.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on a click in the engine's account creation window.

label: Country list
summary: The list of countries the account sign-up form offers.
details: The game names no return type. Vanilla fills a list of the account creation window from it, whose entries show their country names.

label: Day list
summary: The list of days the account sign-up form offers to pick from.
details: The game names no return type. Vanilla fills a list of the account creation window from it. Going by the matching month and year lists, it is part of a date (likely the birth date) picker.

label: Email
summary: The email address in the account sign-up form, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a field in the engine's account creation window.

label: Error message
summary: The error text of the account sign-up form, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in the engine's account creation window. When it is filled is not described.

label: Month list
summary: The list of months the account sign-up form offers to pick from.
details: The game names no return type. Vanilla fills a list of the account creation window from it, next to the day and year lists.

label: Marketing opt-in ticked
summary: Whether the marketing opt-in box of the account sign-up form is ticked.
details: Vanilla ticks a check box of the engine's account creation window with it.

label: Password
summary: The password in the account sign-up form, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a field in the engine's account creation window.

label: Selected country
summary: Which entry of the country list in the account sign-up form is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the selected entry of the country list. The game lists its return type as a pair of whole numbers rather than a single one; what the pair holds is not described.

label: Selected day
summary: Which entry of the day list in the account sign-up form is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the selected entry of the day list. The game lists its return type as a pair of whole numbers rather than a single one; what the pair holds is not described.

label: Selected month
summary: Which entry of the month list in the account sign-up form is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the selected entry of the month list. The game lists its return type as a pair of whole numbers rather than a single one; what the pair holds is not described.

label: Selected year
summary: Which entry of the year list in the account sign-up form is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the selected entry of the year list. The game lists its return type as a pair of whole numbers rather than a single one; what the pair holds is not described.

label: Year list
summary: The list of years the account sign-up form offers to pick from.
details: The game names no return type. Vanilla fills a list of the account creation window from it, next to the day and month lists.

label: Hide sign-up window
summary: Hides the account sign-up window.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on a click in the engine's account creation window.

label: Is creating account
summary: Whether the account is being created right now, after the form was sent off.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a part of the account creation window only while this is under way.

label: Country changed
summary: Takes in the country the player picked in the account sign-up form.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when the selection of the country list changes.

label: Day changed
summary: Takes in the day the player picked in the account sign-up form.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when the selection of the day list changes.

label: Month changed
summary: Takes the month the player picked in the birth date month list of the account sign-up form.
details: Vanilla runs it when the selection of the month dropdown changes, in the engine's Paradox account sign-up window. The year and day dropdowns next to it run their own functions. It returns nothing.

label: Marketing opt-in toggled
summary: Switches the marketing opt-in of the account sign-up form on or off.
details: Vanilla runs it when the player clicks the check box for marketing messages in the engine's Paradox account sign-up window; the box shows its state through a separate function. It returns nothing.

label: Year changed
summary: Takes the year the player picked in the birth date year list of the account sign-up form.
details: Vanilla runs it when the selection of the year dropdown changes, in the engine's Paradox account sign-up window. It returns nothing.

label: Create account itself
summary: The create account object itself, for passing it to other functions.
details: Going by its name, and by how other types use Self (for example Character.Self as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Set email
summary: Takes the text typed into the email box as the email address of the account sign-up form.
details: Vanilla runs it each time the text of the email box changes; the edit box passes its text itself, so no argument is written. It returns nothing.

label: Set password
summary: Takes the text typed into the password box as the password of the account sign-up form.
details: Vanilla runs it each time the text of the password box changes; the edit box passes its text itself, so no argument is written. It returns nothing.

label: Show sign-up
summary: Shows the account sign-up window.
details: Vanilla never uses it on this type; the lines of other types that use a Show are unrelated texts. This rests on the name only.

label: Claimant faction window itself
summary: Hands back the claimant faction window it is called on, for passing on to other functions.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the window itself. Vanilla has no use of it on this type, so this rests on the name only.

label: Can send offer
summary: Whether the request to create the claimant faction can be sent now.
details: Vanilla enables the send buttons only when this is true.

label: Clear recipient
summary: Clears the recipient (the character chosen as the other party) in the window.
details: Vanilla runs it from button clicks in the claimant faction window.

label: Close claimant faction window
summary: Closes the claimant faction window.
details: Vanilla runs it from button clicks in that window.

label: Confirmation window
summary: The confirmation part of the window, where the chosen character interaction is shown.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a section of the window.

label: Character selection list
summary: The list used to pick the character the claimant faction is created against.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the selection part of the window. Going by its name, it holds the characters to choose from.

label: Selected title
summary: The title entry the player has picked in the window.
details: Vanilla reads the actual title from it and uses that as a data context.

label: Send offer tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the send button of the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of the send buttons.

label: Titles to choose from
summary: The list of titles the player can pick one from.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of a list in the window, so one row is made per title.

label: Has titles
summary: Whether there are any titles to choose from.
details: Vanilla negates it to show a part of the window when the list is empty.

label: Is title selected
summary: Whether the player has picked a title in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it to show later parts of the window only after a title is picked, and also together with a valid recipient.

label: Claimant faction window itself
summary: The claimant faction window itself, for passing it to other functions.
details: Going by its name, and by how other types use Self (for example Character.Self as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Send
summary: Sends the request to create the claimant faction.
details: Vanilla runs it from the window's send buttons. Going by the window's other functions, it uses the chosen title and character.

label: Create faction entry itself
summary: Hands back the create faction entry it is called on, for passing on to other functions.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the entry itself. Vanilla has no use of it on this type, so this rests on the name only.

label: Create faction tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the button that creates a faction.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the factions window.

label: Can create faction
summary: Whether the player can create this faction now.
details: Vanilla enables the create button in the factions window only when this is true.

label: Create faction
summary: Creates the faction for the player.
details: Vanilla runs it from the create button in the factions window.

label: Create faction text
summary: The label text of the create faction button.
details: Vanilla uses it as text in the factions window.

label: Is shown
summary: Whether this create faction entry is shown in the list.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility of the entry in the factions window.

label: Create faction entry itself
summary: The create faction entry itself, for passing it to other functions.
details: Going by its name, and by how other types use Self (for example Character.Self as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Create profile window itself
summary: Hands back the social profile window it is called on, for passing on to other functions.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the window itself. Vanilla has no use of it on this type, so this rests on the name only.

label: Create profile
summary: Creates the social profile with the name typed in the window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the window's create button and when the player presses Enter in the name box. The button is only active while the name is valid and no profile is being created yet. It returns nothing.

label: Error message
summary: The error text of the create social profile window, empty when there is no error.
details: Vanilla shows the error part of the window only while this text is not empty.

label: Profile name
summary: The profile name typed in the create social profile window, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in the window's name box; typing changes it through SetName.

label: Close profile window
summary: Closes the create social profile window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the window's close button and its Cancel button. It returns nothing.

label: Is creating profile
summary: Whether the profile is being created right now, after the player asked for it.
details: Vanilla shows a waiting sign while it is true and keeps the create button disabled then, so the request is not sent twice.

label: Is valid name
summary: Whether the profile name typed in the window is acceptable.
details: Vanilla enables the create button only while this is true and no profile is being created.

label: Create profile window itself
summary: The social profile window itself, for passing it to other functions.
details: Going by its name, and by how other types use Self (for example Character.Self as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Set profile name
summary: Takes the text typed into the name box as the new profile name.
details: Vanilla runs it each time the text of the name box changes; the edit box passes its text itself, so no argument is written. It returns nothing.

label: Should be shown
summary: Whether the create social profile window should be shown now.
details: Vanilla has no use of it on this type. A map icon uses a function of the same name on its own type for its visibility, which is only a hint.

label: Show profile window
summary: Shows the create social profile window.
details: Vanilla never uses it on this type; the lines of other types that use a Show are unrelated texts. This rests on the name only.

label: Credit portrait itself
summary: Hands back the credit portrait entry it is called on, for passing on to other functions.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the entry itself. Vanilla has no use of it on this type, so this rests on the name only.

label: Bookmark portrait
summary: The bookmark portrait shown for this entry in the credits.
details: Vanilla asks it for a picture of a given environment and camera, sized to the widget, and uses that as a texture in the credits window.

label: Credit text
summary: The text shown with this portrait in the credits.
details: Vanilla uses it as text in the credits window.

label: Credit portrait itself
summary: The credit portrait entry itself, for passing it to other functions.
details: Going by its name, and by how other types use Self (for example Character.Self as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Credits window itself
summary: Hands back the credits window it is called on, for passing on to other functions.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the window itself. Vanilla has no use of it on this type, so this rests on the name only.

label: Credits text
summary: The credits of the game, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it as the text of the credits window.
